newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar expected to be top-heavy in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar expected to be top-heavy in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be top-heavy against the yen in Asia on Monday, with the market cautious about the possibility of yen-supportive comments from a meeting of the Japan-U.S. Business Council in San Francisco later in the day, dealers said.
They said wariness over Japan's growing trade surplus ahead of the release of Japan's current account surplus for May on Wednesday was also a factor to prevent active dollar buying.
"I don't see any buying factors today," a trust bank dealer said. Dealers said they would also focus on Japan's June first 20-day trade surplus data due at 8.50 am (2350 GMT on Sunday).
But they said the impact of this data may be more limited than that of the current account.
"Sales by exporters and Japanese investors for hedge purposes near 115 yen will keep weighing on the dollar," a dealer at a city bank said.
The trust bank dealer said the greenback would be heavy near 114.20-30 yen, while no substantial bids had been detected so far.
"We will be watching carefully any comments from officials at the Japan-U.S. Business Council on currencies," the trust bank dealer said.
